hardinessNote: Fully hardy throughout the UK, tolerating severe winter cold. Foliage may become sparse in harsh winters.
visual: Fast-spreading carpet of bright silver leaves with narrow green margins, topped by whorls of pink-magenta, hooded flowers in late spring and summer.
pest: Generally pest-free. Slugs and snails may occasionally damage tender growth.
aspect: North, East or West-facing; partial to full shade.
soil: Moist but well-drained chalk, clay, loam or sandy soil; tolerates acid, neutral and alkaline conditions.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging. Can spread vigorously in fertile, moist soil. Water during establishment in dry shade.
water: Water regularly until established. Afterwards water during extended dry spells, especially beneath trees or in containers.
prune: Trim after flowering to encourage fresh silver foliage. Cut back wandering stems and divide overcrowded patches in spring or autumn.
resilience: Extremely cold-hardy, shade-tolerant and adaptable. Established plants tolerate moderate dry shade and recover readily from cutting back.
uses: Shade groundcover, woodland gardens, underplanting shrubs, edging, banks, wildlife planting, hanging baskets and containers.
pollination: Bee-friendly flowers providing nectar for visiting pollinators.
uncertain: Evergreen persistence varies with winter severity; some nursery descriptions classify the plant as dying back in winter.
Flowering duration varies by climate, with occasional flowers continuing into late summer.
Numeric care and light scores are horticultural estimates.

hardinessNote: Exact cultivar hardiness is unverified. Protect from hard frost and winter waterlogging. Overwinter container plants in a cool, frost-free location for reliable survival.
visual: Compact, bushy autumn-flowering chrysanthemum with masses of small, densely petalled purple to violet-pink blooms above dark green, deeply lobed foliage.
pest: Watch for aphids, spider mites, earwigs and leaf miners. Chrysanthemum white rust, grey mould and powdery mildew may occur.
aspect: South or West-facing; full sun in a warm, sheltered position.
soil: Fertile, moisture-retentive but well-drained loam or multipurpose peat-free compost.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogged soil, prolonged drought and deep shade. Container-grown plants are particularly vulnerable to winter frost.
water: Keep evenly moist during active growth and flowering. Water when the compost surface begins to dry, avoiding prolonged saturation.
prune: Deadhead spent flowers regularly. Pinch young growth to encourage branching. After flowering, cut stems to approximately 20 cm before winter storage.
toxicity: Potentially harmful to cats and dogs if eaten. Chrysanthemums can also cause skin irritation or allergic reactions when handled.
resilience: Suited to cool autumn conditions and seasonal displays. Winter survival depends on cultivar hardiness, drainage and protection from severe frost.
uses: Autumn patio pots, seasonal bedding, window boxes, container arrangements, hanging basket displays and sheltered sunny borders.
stockForm: Compact, densely branched flowering pot plant
pollination: Fully double flowers may provide limited access to pollen and nectar compared with single-flowered chrysanthemums.
uncertain: A Dutch wholesale listing confirms the retail designation 'Belgian Mums Soul Sister Purple', but Gediflora's official Soul Sister catalogue does not list Purple as a separate named colour. Exact cultivar identity requires confirmation.
Height and spread are estimates based on compact Soul Sister pot-grown plants rather than verified mature dimensions for Purple.
Autumn flowering period is inferred from the Soul Sister series; flowering time depends on production scheduling and climate.
No cultivar-specific RHS hardiness rating was established.
Purple flower colour is based on the retail designation; exact shade requires confirmation.
Numeric care and light scores are horticultural estimates.
